blurb: Smallest of Japan's six native breeds, a fox-like brushwood hunting dog
description: The Shiba Inu is a small-to-medium Japanese hunting dog with a double coat in red, sesame or black and tan, known as alert, independent and strong-willed.
answer: The Shiba Inu is a Japanese hunting dog and the smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan. Its name means 'brushwood dog', and it was bred to flush small game in mountainous country. It is a small-to-medium breed described as alert, affectionate and independent, but also stubborn.

body: The Shiba is considered a basal breed that predates modern 19th-century breeds, and dogs resembling it appear in prehistoric Jōmon-period figurines. It hunted birds and rabbits in the mountains of the Chūbu region. Crossbreeding with imported Western dogs after the Meiji Restoration left almost no pure Shiba by the 1920s.

Wartime food shortages and later distemper outbreaks nearly wiped the breed out, and modern Shibas come from three surviving bloodlines: Shinshu, Mino and San'in. The first standard was published in 1934, and in 1936 the Shiba was declared a Natural Monument of Japan. The American Kennel Club recognized it in 1992.

Standard colors are red, sesame and black and tan, all with cream to white markings called urajiro on the muzzle, cheeks, chest, legs, belly and underside of the tail. A cream coat is considered a major fault by the Japan Kennel Club, AKC and FCI, but is accepted by The Kennel Club in the UK. The double coat has a stiff topcoat and a soft, plush undercoat; long-haired Shibas occur rarely through a recessive gene.

The Shiba is commonly described as alert, affectionate and independent, with high intelligence but a stubborn, strong-willed streak. Japanese standards stress spirited boldness, good nature and artlessness. One expert survey rated it high in aggression and reactivity and medium in trainability, and the breed has a reputation for being aloof, so early socialization is emphasized.

Sources say the breed needs plenty of exercise and mental stimulation, and that too little can lead to anxiety and unwanted behavior such as the so-called shiba scream. It copes well with mountainous terrain and hiking trails.

Conditions reported in the breed include patellar luxation, glaucoma, canine atopic dermatitis, a Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome and GM1 gangliosidosis. The breed is long-lived: a Japanese cemetery review found a life expectancy of 15.5 years, and a 2024 UK study found 14.6 years.

faq.a: The name literally translates as 'brushwood dog', referring to its use flushing game from brush. Inu is Japanese for dog.

faq.q: How long do Shiba Inus live?
faq.a: The Shiba is one of the longer-lived breeds: a Japanese study found 15.5 years and a 2024 UK study 14.6 years.
They have a double coat with a soft, plush undercoat beneath stiff guard hairs. Sources give little detail on shedding, but double-coated breeds generally need regular brushing.

faq.q: Is the Shiba Inu the Doge meme dog?
faq.a: Yes. The 2013 Doge meme featured Kabosu, a Shiba Inu, and the Dogecoin cryptocurrency logo shows her image.
